Message.text: Castle Graymantle, three tiers of gray stone on a sea cliff. The road runs north to the bridge. The wind off the water smells of salt and old iron.
Graymantle Bridge. A knight in gray holds it, they say: Corvane, who fenced every traveler who tried to cross. A stair cut into the cliff beside the bridge runs down under its deck.
The cliff path. It runs under the bridge, narrow, with the sea far below. It ends at the Barbican's cistern. Mind the edge.
The Barbican cistern. A stair at the east wall climbs to the courtyard. The gatehouse lever is up there, by the main gate.
The main gate bars the bridge from this side. The lever beside it lifts the bar. Once it is open, the road back to the Lantern across the bridge is short.
The Lower Ward. A kennel on the west, an armory on the east, a chapel beyond it. A ladder climbs to the wall-walk. The main stair to the keep is straight ahead, and it is guarded.
The armory. Racks of gray plate and greatshields. One chest here sits crooked: its latch is on the wrong side.
A ballista crouches on the wall above, its bolts rusted in the rack. The wall-walk is reached by the ladder to the north, and it leads on, past the archers, toward the ramparts.
The stair to the keep. Two Gray Knights keep it. Their shields are high, so strike low and wide, or bash the guard open.

The windward court, the castle's third tier. The wind comes straight off the sea. Archers hold a perch on each wall, and a captain in gray plate keeps the east end. The keep's door stands ahead. A stair along its west wall climbs to the library's other door.
A lift cage hangs in the corner of the bastion. Its door opens only from inside. Ride it down once and the Lower Ward is a short walk from the Lantern at the bridge.
The keep. The dining hall lies inside, and above it the library. The scholars say a table is still laid.
A feast no one finished. The servants at the benches have sat a long time. The best of the table lies on the high board, and they do not like it taken.

The Graymantle library. The shelves are in order and the readers are not. A ladder at the south wall climbs to the upper shelf. A faint hum comes from the east wall, behind the last case. The north door leads on to the bell tower and the Castellan's hall.
A faint hum, behind this wall.

The bell tower. The stair winds twice around an open well to the belfry. The bell cracked long ago, and the wind plays what is left. A scroll on the belfry floor teaches a parry for weapons that cannot parry.
The Castellan's antechamber. The hall lies through the gap in the north wall. Voss has fought every duel in this castle, and he remembers all of them. Vary your play.
The back gate stays shut while the Castellan lives. Beyond it the road climbs to Rimeshelf.
The pass north. Snow has drifted against the wall, and the wind is colder.
